owner: orchestrator (no print engineer dispatched; DIRECT-style single-part job)

support_rules.allowed_contact_class: non-functional exterior: the upper leg's flat inner side face (z=35mm, ~1440mm2) and the ball's lower spherical cap plus the plinth underside (~150mm2). No support may touch a vent claw profile edge, a snap-bore wall, or the phone-rest face.
forbidden_faces: the two snap bores through the leg tabs and their barrel walls
every vent-claw prong tip and prong flank
post_print_artifacts: photo of the sphere after support removal and knife/400-grit cleanup
photo of the upper leg's inner face after support removal
arm snap-in test: the untouched solid[1] arm must seat and pivot freely

interfaces.contact_state: ball gripped by the user's existing MagSafe cradle socket, held by friction
interfaces.motion_path: none once seated; the cradle rotates about the ball centre
interfaces.material: PETG ball against the user's existing printed socket
interfaces.acceptance_method: Nobody has the cradle's geometry, so the band is not a socket clearance. The reference is the source ball STL's own spherical cap moved exactly as the graft moves it, and the band asserts congruence: the delivered sphere must still be the validated sphere, within 0.05 mm, after a plinth was fused under it. Vertex sphere d 17.140, centre 22.080 mm off the phone-rest face.

interfaces.contact_state: the vent arm's peg seated in the leg's barrel bore and free to pivot
interfaces.motion_path: peg pressed in along the bore axis past a 0.44 mm radial interference at the mouth, then free rotation
interfaces.acceptance_method: Band derived from the two source solids' own surface parameters before measuring: bore r 2.000 -> 2.600 -> 2.000 against peg r 1.900 -> 2.440 -> 1.900 gives a 0.100 mm minimum radial gap at the mouths and 0.160 at the barrel; this build's 0.020 mm mouth relief raises the minimum to 0.120. Anything outside 0.09-0.18 means the bore rebuild moved.
